## Overview

Confluent Inc. is the commercial company founded by the creators of Apache Kafka. Confluent Cloud provides Apache Kafka as a fully managed service with Schema Registry, connectors, stream processing (ksqlDB, Flink), and governance features. Confluent Schema Registry is the market-leading schema registry for event-driven architectures, supporting Avro, JSON Schema, and Protobuf with server-side validation and compatibility enforcement.

## Products & Services

- **Confluent Cloud** — Fully managed Apache Kafka with multiple cluster types (Basic, Standard, Enterprise, Dedicated, Freight). Available on AWS, Azure, and GCP.
- **Confluent Schema Registry** — Schema storage, versioning, and compatibility enforcement. Server-side validation at the producer. Supports Avro, JSON Schema, Protobuf.
- **Confluent Control Center** — Monitoring and management console for Kafka clusters.
- **ksqlDB / Apache Flink** — Stream processing for real-time data transformation and analytics.
- **Confluent Connectors** — Pre-built connectors for common data sources and sinks.

## Pricing Model

- **Basic cluster**: USD $50-$300/month (dev/test)
- **Standard cluster**: USD $1,000-$3,000/month (small production)
- **Enterprise cluster**: USD $5,000-$20,000/month (mid-size with governance)
- **Dedicated cluster**: USD $10,000-$50,000+/month (2+ CKUs)
- **Schema Registry (Essentials)**: 100 free schemas; USD $0.002/schema/hour thereafter
- **Schema Registry (Advanced)**: USD $1/hour; 20,000 included schemas; 99.99% SLA
- Exact CKU rates are not publicly disclosed; require sales engagement.

**Confidence**: MEDIUM (3-4 data points; CKU pricing not publicly disclosed)

## Australian Presence

- Australian data centres: YES — Available on AWS ap-southeast-2 (Sydney) and Azure Australia East
- Schema Registry available in Australian regions: YES

## Government Award History

> Not applicable. Australian university context. No UK procurement data.

## Strengths

- Market-leading schema registry with server-side validation — strongest enforcement model
- Full event replay from any offset — strongest recovery and audit capability
- Exactly-once semantics (EOS) for guaranteed delivery
- Large and active community; extensive training and certification programme
- Multi-cloud availability (AWS, Azure, GCP)
- Australian region confirmed
- Open-source Apache Kafka protocol — low lock-in at the data plane

## Weaknesses

- New purchase — fails Principle 19 for this project (existing Azure capability must be evaluated first)
- Significantly more expensive than Azure under the existing agreement (estimated 40-100% more)
- Kafka operational concepts (partitions, consumer groups, offsets) have a steeper learning curve
- CKU pricing is opaque — requires sales engagement for exact rates
- Over-engineered for the university's event volume ( < 10,000 events/day)
- Managed service dependency on Confluent — vendor viability risk (though Confluent is well-funded)
